$comment: Binaries this application trusts to load into its own process (ADR-047).
tdjson sees the Telegram session key, every message and the network, so an
entry here is a statement that someone established where the file came from.
An empty list is the correct initial state: nothing is trusted yet, and
`tgassist tdlib verify` prints the entry to add once a binary is obtained.
Review a change to this file as you would any other security change. A
digest recorded from whatever happened to be on disk makes the whole
Fields: platform (system-machine), sha256 (of the whole file), version
(optional; cross-checked against what the library reports), source (where
it came from, in your own words), recorded (ISO date).

entries.source: Built from source with scripts/build-tdjson.bat: tdlib/td commit 022d60202e446ad1287b9fb68e687c8a0760788b, MSVC 19.51.36248 (VS 18 Enterprise, toolset 14.51.36231), CMake 4.3.1 + Ninja, Release, vcpkg x64-windows-static OpenSSL 3.6.3 and zlib 1.3.2 built from source and linked statically. Verified self-contained: no OpenSSL or zlib runtime dependency (dumpbin /dependents). Needs the Visual C++ redistributable.
